ambiguityScan.note: The fix's expected behaviour admits one reading. The two orderings do not compete: a filter change after a page change resets to page 1 (GH-1 AC6), and a page change after a filter change lands on page 2 of the filtered list (GH-1 AC1). Two rapid writes to different keys both land; two to the same key resolve last-write-wins, which is what the user's second action asked for. #3 carries no Gherkin because ticket-standard has no bug variant - a known gap in that standard - so the acceptance criteria are derived in the spec from GH-1's AC1 and AC6, which are the ACs the defect contradicts.

round3.b1Evidence: Established rather than assumed. No pending state exists in the delivered code - read() at use-latest-ticket-list-params.ts:44-51 is a pure closure over the router navigator, so there is nothing to resurrect from. The regression guard was run against cda1c03's pending-write mechanism and failed with the exact value round 2 reported (expected '?search=login&page=2' to be '?page=2', 1 failed / 238 passed), so it pins the class and not this implementation. One residue found and dismissed: under BrowserRouter globalHistory.go(-1) is async while createMemoryHistory.go is synchronous, leaving a one-task window the memory-history guard cannot observe - but two user input events are two tasks and the traversal task queues first, so a reader cannot land a click inside it. Unlike round 2's, it is not persistent state.
blockers: B-R3-1. TicketsPage.tsx:49-55 - the refiningExistingSearch live read is unguarded. Reverting its five operands from `current` to `params` leaves the full suite at 242/242. Probed: two fireEvent.change on the search box inside one act give navigationType REPLACE delivered vs PUSH mutated, and one Back lands on '' vs '?search=l' - i.e. Back walking the reader through logi/log/lo, which is exactly what GH-1's CASE-222fa42cb560 exists to prevent. That case uses user.type, which serialises, so it cannot see the same-render window. The spec (GH-3-spec.md:131-133) states this change is required or the history rule GH-1 established silently regresses; a delivered change whose named regression class survives all 242 tests is round 1's blocker 1 at a fourth call site.

B-R3-2. use-latest-ticket-list-params.ts:48 - the B1 guard is one-sided. Mutating `live?.search === undefined` to `!live?.search` leaves the suite at 242/242, and probing entries ['/tickets','/tickets?status=open'] at initialIndex 1 with navigate(-1) and Next in one act gives '?page=2' delivered vs '?status=open&page=2' mutated - round-2 B1's exact symptom. The existing guard at TicketsPage.test.tsx:1857 cannot see it because its POP lands on the default URL, where the committed params and the parsed-empty-search result are identical. The distinguishing case - POP target bare, committed params not - has no test.

B-R3-3. Two writes to different filter keys in one render still lose one. Probed against delivered code: status=open then search=login gives '?search=login' (status lost); the reverse order gives '?status=open' (search lost). Cause is outside the files GH-3 changed: TicketsFilters.tsx:31,39,58 build nextFilters as {...filters, <one key>} from the COMMITTED filter set, so all three keys are always present and always stale, and TicketsPage.tsx:60's {...current, ...nextFilters} overwrites the live values with them. This is a real unfixed defect in GH-3's own intent, not a test gap. It contradicts three spec claims: 'so no write is lost' (:18), 'Two rapid writes to different keys both land' (:62-63), and 'TicketsFilters.tsx is not changed: it already passes deltas outward' (:147-148) - it passes the whole set, not a delta. Recon named this exact pair at GH-3-recon.md:50 ('filter A + filter B') and :56 ('Every pair of writes is affected: ... filter+filter').

B-R3-4. GH-3-spec.md:214-216 attributes E2E evidence to the deleted mechanism. The spec reports 'three full runs: 81/82, 82/82, 82/82'; the state file records five runs, and those three are exactly the ones tagged atMechanism 'pending-write queue'. The two runs tagged 'live location' - the only ones measuring the delivered code - do not appear in the spec, nor does the flake's mechanism context. decisionNeeded: D-R3-1. The private-API containment does not cover a change of router type. Measured in react-router 7.13.0: BrowserRouter and MemoryRouter both pass a history whose `location` is a live getter, but RouterProvider / createBrowserRouter passes a navigator of {createHref, encodeLocation, go, push, replace} with no location at all, and the declared Navigator type has no location member (which is why the cast exists). So a migration to a data router activates the fallback in production while every component test keeps mounting MemoryRouter and stays green - including the hook's own live-read tests, which inject a hand-built navigator and never mount a real router. GH-3 would regress with a fully green suite. The spec's claim that such an upgrade 'fails a test naming this file' holds for a version bump that removes the getter (it fails the two page-level race tests, which name TicketsPage, not the hook), and not at all for a router-type change. Separately: the fallback is unreachable under both routers installed today, since history.location.search is always a string - it is tested future-proofing, not dead code, but production never exercises it.

Enumerated: AC-a has 4 behaviour classes and 1 scenario (inside another AC's case), AC-b has 2 and none, AC-c has 2 and none, AC-d has 1 and none. The checklist's full-delta rule makes this a blocker; CLAUDE.md pulls the other way (component-first, never duplicate component coverage in E2E), the race is component-testable and mutation-proven there, and the spec already routes the question to the gate.
